free_tier.stated: Free compute on fal's inference platform. The route is an email to grants@fal.ai with a project description, goals, and 'any relevant work or GitHub repositories'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The grant is platform credit, so it composes only with fal's own models; it is a supplement for an inference-heavy step, not a training allowance.

limits.value: the award has no published amount, cap, duration or expiry, so the only thing bounding it is a discretionary reply to an email.

evidence.proved: 'open to anyone passionate about advancing AI through open source projects'; 'simply reach out to us at grants@fal.ai'; quoted; page 200

the page publishes no amount, no duration and no expiry; the only evidence of awards is two named testimonials (Vik Korrapati for Moondream, Peng Zheng for BiRefNet), which show the program paid out to identifiable people but carry no figure

notes: Recorded for the door rather than the number, and it is honest to say so: no figure exists on the page, so the finding cannot rank against Lambda or TRC. What makes it worth a line is the explicit removal of the degree requirement in a class where nearly every other program gates on it, plus the fact that the application is an email rather than a form. The named testimonials are the only proof it pays out. Whether the credits are GPU-seconds on fal's inference endpoints or spend on the platform is not stated, and that distinction decides whether a training run is possible at all - it probably is not, which is the caveat.
